Selected technical work / Remote sensing & AI

Forecasting inundation
from satellite time series.

A VAE3 spatiotemporal experiment in coastal Satkhira, Bangladesh. Four historical water masks are used to predict the next observed inundation pattern, followed by held-out evaluation and explainability analysis.

Case study · VAE3
0.743Held-out wet-class F1
0.590Held-out wet-class IoU
1,244Evaluated temporal patch samples

Research question

Can past inundation masks anticipate the next one?

The model was trained with 128 × 128 binary wet/dry patches from three Satkhira-area unions. It learns from four earlier observations to estimate the next available inundation mask.

Unlike a conventional flood simulation, this approach learns temporal patterns directly from satellite-derived classifications. Because imagery dates are irregular, the forecast represents the next observation, not a fixed 7-day or monthly lead time.

Study settingThree coastal union areas, Satkhira, Bangladesh
InputsFour earlier binary inundation masks, 128 × 128 pixels
ApproachVAE3 · TensorFlow / Keras · chronological holdout
ReferenceAlgorithmically derived wet/dry masks, not independently surveyed flood extents

Method in brief

From past observations to a probability map.

01 / Data

Prepare spatial sequences

Align historical binary masks, screen valid patch windows, and assemble four-frame temporal inputs.

02 / Learning

Train and calibrate VAE3

Train with chronological validation and select a wet-probability threshold from validation results.

03 / Assessment

Predict and inspect

Test on later dates, compare with persistence, and examine temporal contributions using XAI.

Recorded performance

A promising signal, with an important trade-off.

The VAE3 experiment slightly improved wet-class F1 and IoU compared with carrying forward the last observed mask. However, it produced more false positives, lower overall accuracy, and a substantial overestimation of wet area.

For research communication, this is best presented as a completed experimental result with clear limitations, not as a validated operational forecasting system.

These scores describe agreement with satellite-derived pseudo-labels, after filtering some pure dry/wet patches. Independent field validation was not part of this recorded experiment.

Model interpretation

What the model attends to across time.

Temporal ablation and integrated gradients offer exploratory views of how the four historical frames influence the VAE3 output. These analyses illustrate model behaviour rather than establish physical flood drivers.

Research record

Reproducible code, visible results, and clearly stated limits.

The public release includes the VAE3 notebook, saved figures and recorded metrics. Raw satellite imagery, georeferenced labels and training checkpoints are not included. The corresponding code repository must be published separately before a direct project link is available.
